subject: P9 built: 0104 gated CPU DVFS (n2cpu) + 0105 handles 256->1024 (render lead: bridge MAX_BO 256 must follow); run_all.sh green
body: gpu/build/device-mmu-p9-candidate/manifest.json; README-0104-0105.md; run_all.sh: 7 FINAL + 6 XNU + 2 MODEL PASS, 32/32 source files identical stage vs candidate tree. Kernels A' 01209f6a (0099a+0104) / B' 7f0d41f9 (0099a+b+0104). Images: ui654fb60 97d890d5 (595 chars, n2fbhz=60) ; ui654fb60cpu 008025c7 (606, n2fbhz=60 n2cpu=2000) ; ui654fb60ab 3e832af8 (604, kernel B', n2fbhz=60 n2sch=15) ; probe350 7e889255 (595, n2csram=1, metal 0). Patches 0104 bdc00ec8, 0105 9fe327f9. 0105 FINDING for the render lead: the 257th small buffer failed with N2C_E_VA because the per-context free-VA-extent list had 256 slots (64 KiB-aligned small BOs leave a gap each) - raised to 1032 with the handle table to 1024 (handle = serial<<10|slot, serial now 22 bits = 4.19M buffers per boot, fail-closed). gpu/metal/nord2_metal_bridge.c has its own #define MAX_BO 256 (struct bo bos[MAX_BO]) which still caps the bridge at 256: raise it to 1024 to stop the command drops; I did not touch your file. WHAT EACH IMAGE PROVES: probe350 = the CSRAM dump is not enabled here (n2csram=1 only prints the same 9 words; the full 0x1400 dump needs n2cpu>=1); it re-measures CPUCLK on the new kernel. ui654fb60 = baseline for kernel A' at 60 Hz: PRESENT line timing (copy 2.3-3 ms + xfer 10.4 ms vs 16.7 ms period), SWAPWAIT line, CPUCLK unchanged (big cores ~730), n2cpu inert. ui654fb60cpu = the ONLY image that can change CPU clocks: it logs the whole CSRAM, each candidate block and verdict; if a cpufreq-hw domain verifies it ramps cpu4-6/cpu7 to <=2000 MHz row by row with a measured check per row; if nothing verifies it writes nothing (expected outcome if the MT6893 firmware is not running or uses the legacy cpuhvfs interface) and the dump is the deliverable. Compare CPUCLK lines before/after (n2clk 300 s; kern.nord2_cpuclk on demand). ui654fb60ab = kernel B' with placement mode 0xf always on and the per-switch accounting hooked (NORD2 SCHED lines become meaningful for the first time: big/little busy %, backboardd watch). Not proven by any image: that the gauge-only thermal guard is enough at 2.0 GHz (no SoC sensor), that PERF_STATE writes are honoured by this firmware.
